correspondences.rationale: Both denote a physical fibre break that prevents light propagation.
Both denote increased attenuation on a fibre span, such as from bending or cable stress.
Both denote an unplugged connector or patch cord that breaks optical continuity.
Both denote connector contamination that introduces optical loss or degradation.
Both denote pump-laser or complete amplifier failure resulting in no optical output.
Both denote amplifier gain falling below its configured value.
Both denote increased amplifier-added noise or noise figure, reducing OSNR.
Both denote a non-flat amplifier gain profile across the optical band.
Both denote progressive pump ageing evidenced by increasing pump drive current.
Both denote failure of a coherent line transmitter's laser.
Both denote a hard equipment-card failure.
Both denote local coherent-receiver deterioration that adds a receive penalty.
Both denote drift of a WSS attenuation setting for an individual channel.
Both denote frequency misalignment of a WSS passband for one channel.
Both denote hard failure of a WSS port; model A specifically identifies the degree input port.
Both denote increased differential group delay on the fibre path.
Both denote a rapid transient change in optical state of polarization.
Both denote failure of an OTN switch's ODU cross-connect fabric.
Both denote an erroneous OTN cross-connect that sends an ODU to the wrong destination.
Both denote failure of a client port or its client optic.
Both denote absence of detectable optical light at the receiver.
Both denote reduced optical signal power.
Both denote section-local loss of the OSC, which is terminated and regenerated at amplifier sites.
Both denote reduced optical signal-to-noise ratio on affected channels.
Both denote polarization changing rapidly enough to cause a transient receiver impairment.
Both denote an internally failed unit whose traffic and valid monitoring are lost or suppressed.
Both denote loss of OTU frame alignment at the line receiver.
Both denote pre-FEC errors above the signal-degrade threshold while framing remains available.
Both denote an ODU Alarm Indication Signal propagating downstream.
Both denote an ODU delivered to the wrong destination by a cross-connect.
Both denote interruption or unavailability of the client service.
Both denote a brief client-service interruption during protection switching.
Both describe increasing pump drive current to maintain amplifier gain as the pump ages.
Both are aggregate optical-power measurements at an amplifier input.
Both are aggregate optical-power measurements at an amplifier output.
Both measure pump drive current as a percentage of beginning-of-life current.
Both are per-channel optical-power measurements from ROADM channel monitoring.
Both are per-channel OSNR measurements from ROADM channel monitoring.
Both denote optical power measured at a line receiver.
Both are line errored-second counts reported in 15-minute performance bins.
Both denote OSNR estimated by a coherent receiver or DSP.
Both denote the coherent receiver's pre-FEC bit error ratio.
Both denote receiver-estimated differential group delay.
Both measure the rate of change of optical state of polarization.
Both are client-interface errored seconds reported in 15-minute bins.
Both are client-interface unavailable seconds reported in 15-minute bins.
Both denote the booster amplifier role at the transmitting end of an OMS.
Both denote an inline amplifier at an intermediate amplifier site.
Both denote the preamplifier role at the receiving end of an OMS.
Both denote the class of coherent line-terminating units, including transponders, muxponders, and OTN line cards.
Both denote a transponder line-interface type.
Both denote a muxponder line-interface type.
Both denote an OTN line-card line-interface type.
Both denote a reconfigurable optical add/drop multiplexer using WSS functions.
Both denote an OTN switch containing an ODU cross-connect fabric.
Both denote a client-facing port that maps client traffic into an ODU.
Both denote every channel in the referenced multiplexed signal or affected set.
Both denote one optical wavelength channel.
Both denote a proper subset of multiplexed channels rather than all channels.
Both denote every channel arriving through one ROADM degree input port.
Both scope a statement to the equipment unit itself rather than its traffic.
Both restrict the scope to the current receiver only.
Both denote every ODU cross-connected through the OTN switch.
Both denote one individual ODU connection.
Both denote the particular client service under discussion.
Both locate a condition at the current alarm-raising or monitored unit.
Both locate a condition at the current alarm-raising port.
Both denote the fibre span immediately upstream of the unit.
Both denote the nearest upstream amplifier feeding the span or unit.
Both denote the input patch or connection of the optical multiplex section.
Both denote the remote line transmitter whose signal is received locally.
Both denote the remote line receiver receiving the current unit's signal.
Both denote the end-to-end signal path between the current and far-end line interfaces.
Both denote either client-facing endpoint of the service.
Both denote an OTN switch or cross-connect lying along the service's ODU path.
Both denote the service's working ODU path.
Both denote the service's protection ODU path.
Both denote the ODU path currently carrying the live service.
Both denote availability of optical-power monitoring when the power option is fitted.
Both denote availability of per-channel power and OSNR from optical channel monitoring.
Both denote advanced coherent-DSP and equipment-health telemetry availability.
Both denote an abrupt hard failure that causes an outage.
Both denote reduced quality while traffic remains carried, rather than an outage.
Both denote a slow pre-failure trend before traffic is affected.
Both denote critical alarm severity.
Both denote major alarm severity.
Both denote minor alarm severity.
Both denote a reported condition that does not raise an alarm.
Both denote passing an arriving condition through without alteration.
Both denote independent per-channel ROADM switching.
